title: Prefill boundary detector and microbenchmark swap policy for safer op-choice transitions
creator: Aisha Fernando
description:
Problem: For mixed prefill/decode traffic we observe cases where switching to a lower-latency kernel mid-request (typically after a prefill boundary) reduces tail latency but can regress correctness or spike p99 when KV warming and memory layout expectations differ. Current heuristics are brittle across architectures and sequence-length distributions.

Proposal: Implement a two-part runtime subsystem: (1) a lightweight prefill-boundary detector that tags requests where the runtime can safely attempt an op-variant swap after prefill (based on token-phase, recent seqlen histogram, and active KV cache state), and (2) a background microbenchmarking service that continuously produces per-(model,arch,seq-len-bucket) swap safety scores derived from short, sandboxed probes. The runtime will consult both signals to decide a soft-swap policy: allow trial switches for a small probe budget, monitor correctness/latency metrics, and either promote the swap path or roll back and blacklist if regressions occur.

Key ideas: lightweight boundary detection avoids probing on short/predictable dialogs; microbench probes run off critical paths and use isolated memory contexts; soft-swap uses warmup KV replay and can fall back intra-request with no user-visible error; we track both latency regressions and deviation in deterministic outputs (hash-based diffs for deterministic ops), with stricter thresholds for non-deterministic ops.

Why unique: instead of a pure heuristic or purely offline autotune, this combines per-request boundary signals with live microbench-derived confidence scores to allow safe, incremental adoption of faster op-variants per-arch and per-seqlen bucket.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes a prefill-boundary detector flag per request and logs a boundary_reason metric
Background microbench service emits swap_safety_score for (model_id, arch, seqlen_bucket) every 10m
Soft-swap policy executes trial swaps for <1% of qualifying requests by default and can be toggled via runtime flags
No user-visible correctness regressions in canary (deterministic op hashes within 1e-6 mismatch rate) and p99 latency improves or remains neutral for targeted workloads
Automated rollback triggers when swapped-path error rate increases by >0.5% or p99 latency degrades by >10% over 5m
implementation_plan: Week 0: Spec and API - define prefill-boundary schema, metric names, and control flags (runtime + console)
Week 1: Implement detector - integrate token-phase hooks and seqlen histogram checks into prefill pipeline
Week 2: Build sandbox microbench harness - isolated process that runs short prefill+decode patterns for model/arch combos
Week 3: Define scoring - combine latency delta, memory copy overhead, and deterministic-output divergence into a swap_safety_score (0-100)
Week 4: Soft-swap runtime path - trial allocation, KV-warmup replay, and safe revert mechanism
Week 5: Telemetry + alarms - dashboards, canary pipeline, and automated rollback rules
Week 6: Canary rollout to internal customers, collect telemetry and iterate
Week 7: Broader rollout with console controls for per-customer opt-in
risks: Probing overhead: microbench probes could consume GPU time if not isolated or throttled
False negatives: detector may miss boundaries and forgo beneficial swaps
Correctness drift: non-deterministic ops (sampling, beam search variants) make output diffs noisy
Operational complexity: added subsystem increases attack surface for regressions and alerts
telemetry: swap_trial_count and swap_promote_count (by model, arch, seqlen_bucket)
p50/p95/p99 latency delta of swapped vs baseline paths
rollout_plan: Start with an internal canary covering a small selection of conversational models and a single architecture (A100-80GB). Enable trial swaps at 0.1% of qualifying requests, monitor telemetry for 48h, then increase to 1% if stable. After 7 days of stable metrics, expand to other archs and customers. Provide per-customer toggle in console and runbook for emergency rollback.
tests: Unit tests for boundary detector heuristics (token-phase variations)
Integration test: soft-swap within a single request with simulated KV state and rollback assertion
E2E canary: deterministic hash diff comparisons for standard prompt set
Load test: microbench probe isolation under 2x production probe budget
design_decisions: We prioritize safety over raw latency: swaps are trial-first and promoted only when microbench and live telemetry agree. Deterministic-output hashing is used where applicable; for sampling/temperature modes we rely more heavily on latency and queueing signals. Microbench samples are budgeted and rate-limited per-GPU to avoid interfering with production throughput.
open_questions: What is the canonical seqlen bucketing strategy across models (fixed buckets vs. percentile-based)?
Should swap_safety_score incorporate historical live rollout feedback or be purely microbench-driven?
What's the safe default probe budget per GPU for multi-tenant clusters?
How to best surface swap recommendations in Console without overwhelming operators?
